answer: A bonded collateral protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock non-refundable deposits in a basalt registry. Nodes maintain standing by answering micro-challenges over a sparrow gossip overlay. Because an attacker cannot mirror authentic network participation without locking scarce liquid capital per identity, scaling fake agents imposes linear financial costs. However, this barrier favors wealthy consortia while penalizing low-budget open-source models.
